heroHeadline: Iran Team Arrives in US for World Cup Opener as Historic Iran-US Peace Deal Announced Simultaneously.
heroSubtitle: The Iran World Cup visa crisis reached a partial resolution on June 6 when the White House confirmed that Iran's players and core athletes received US visas — averting an unprecedented tournament forfeiture. However, 14 backroom officials were denied, including secretary-general Hedayat Mombeini, prompting Iran's Football Federation to accuse the US of 'vindictive behavior.' The squad departed Antalya, Turkey at 6:30 PM on June 6 and arrived at their Centro Xoloitzcuintle base camp in Tijuana, Mexico on the morning of June 7 — 4 days before the June 15 Group G opener vs New Zealand at SoFi Stadium. In pre-tournament friendly action on June 6, Germany defeated host nation USA 2-1 at Soldier Field, Chicago (Havertz 2', Robinson equalizer, Sané 60'); England beat New Zealand 1-0 with a Harry Kane header; Belgium thrashed Tunisia 5-0; and Portugal edged Chile 2-1 with Rafael Leão sent off in a late altercation. Argentina suffered a defensive blow when centre-back Leonardo Balerdi was ruled out with a soleus injury — Marcos Senesi is the leading replacement candidate. On June 7, Lionel Messi sat out Argentina's friendly vs Honduras due to hamstring management, training individually in Kansas City; Scaloni expects him fit for the June 16 Group J opener vs Algeria. Brazil beat Egypt 2-1 but Neymar trained separately — an MRI is scheduled for Monday June 8 as he is doubtful for the June 13 opener vs Morocco. Scotland routed Bolivia 4-0. Canada confirmed Maxime Crépeau as starting goalkeeper. FIFA also cancelled approximately 60 tickets inadvertently issued free via a system glitch, with NY/NJ Attorneys General already probing FIFA's ticketing program. Opening ceremony at Estadio Azteca features Shakira and Burna Boy performing the official song 'Dai Dai.' The tournament opens in 4 days.
